title: Tariff Application Note — Raising Fees on Refined Fuels and Propane Accounts
content:
Fees on an account under Refined Fuels and Propane Accounts are raised on the occasion that gives rise to them and never bundled into the price of the fuel.

1. **Annual tank rent** falls due on the account's rent due date on programmes where the cooperative owns the tank, and it is waived outright for the year where the member's purchases in the twelve months ending on that date reach the programme's waiver gallons. A member just short of the waiver is charged the whole rent and not a part of it.
2. **The regulatory handling charge** is raised once per delivery on programmes that carry it.
3. **An after-hours or emergency stop** carries its fee once per stop, and where a stop is both after hours and off route both fees are charged, because they pay for different things. Fees of different classes add.
4. **The minimum delivery fee** is raised where the gallons pumped fall under the programme's minimum, and it is not raised where the tank simply would not take more.
5. **A fee the catalogue sets at zero** is not raised on that programme at all, and such a fee is not shown as a nil line on the statement.
6. **Reversal.** A fee already charged is reversed only where the stop itself is reversed or where the cooperative's own error caused it.

## The waiver, on both sides of its boundary

The waiver turns on the member's purchases in the twelve months ending on the rent due date, measured against the programme's waiver gallons.

*Hypothetical, at the boundary.* A member on a programme whose waiver stands at 500 gallons has bought exactly 500 gallons in the twelve months ending on the rent due date. The rule reads "reach", so the whole year's rent is waived.

*Hypothetical, just short.* The same member has bought 499 gallons in that window. The rent is not waived in part: the whole rent falls due.

## Stacking, put as a question answered

**A stop was made after hours and off the tank's route. Is one fee charged or two?** Two. The after-hours fee and the out-of-route fee pay for different things, so both are raised on that stop.

**The tank would take only a small load because it was nearly full. Is the minimum delivery fee raised?** No. The fee answers gallons pumped falling under the programme's minimum, and it is not raised where the tank simply would not take more.
